newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to set up free gold market - Chubais.
newsitem.headline: Russia to set up free gold market - Chubais.

text.p: Russian First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais said on Friday that Russia needed radical changes to its gold market, and that a working group would report to him within the next 10 days on concrete steps towards creating a free market.
"We will build a normal, free, regulated gold market in this country," said Chubais, who is also Finance Minister.

"The principal means towards doing that are liberalisation of the gold market...and the formation of a working group of the Finance Ministry, Central Bank and other departments," he told a press briefing.
Chubais provided no further details over how Russia's gold market might be liberalised.
Industry officials have long called for the introduction of radical, market-economy changes in order to shore up falling production levels and to make the system more efficient.
Proposals put forward in recent months included merging many of the smaller gold mines and allowing commercial banks to purchase gold directly from producers.
Russia currently maintains tight control over gold and other precious metals purchases, production and exports.
Estimates on how much gold Russia produces vary widely. A Central Bank official last month put output in 1996 at 122 tonnes, down from 135 tonnes in 1995.
Industry representatives have said that gold production could more than double if more private financing and outside investment could be introduced to the sector.
